summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute worsening of chronic right-sided back, flank, and rib pain over three weeks, along with new-onset severe nausea, vomiting, and early satiety. Pain was managed with IV and oral hydromorphone, and the pain service performed trigger point injections, leading to moderate improvement. Labs showed mild inflammation with CRP of 11 and no evidence of infection, organ dysfunction, or metabolic disturbance. Nausea was not clearly linked to medications or H. pylori and may be related to pain or functional gastrointestinal issues. The patient was transitioned back to his home regimen of oral Dilaudid, omeprazole, and other chronic medications. He was discharged home after three days with stable pain, improved nausea, and plans to follow up in pain clinic and with his PCP for further evaluation of early satiety, possibly including an outpatient endoscopy.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
